title: Chapter 206: She Is My Sister
html:
“Inspector Lee, I found one of the suspects from the psychiatric hospital. She’s hiding at Xin Kang Apartments.” Chen Ge described the woman’s appearance.

“Could you be mistaken? Your description bears no resemblance to the woman we’re seeking. Besides, she doesn’t sound capable of holding anyone captive.”

“Her history closely matches Patient No. 2 from the Third Sick Hall. She may have an accomplice. Either way, I’m at least fifty percent certain.” Worried the driver might overhear and misunderstand, Chen Ge kept his voice low.

“All right. I’ll investigate personally.” Reassured by Inspector Lee’s answer, Chen Ge ended the call. At Fang Hwa Apartments, he slipped through the rear entrance, carefully avoiding the cameras.

The drunk man saw the white figure several months ago, and it moved without a sound. It must be a ghost. Yet despite a ghost living here, Fang Hwa Apartments has reported no injuries in years. Are people concealing the truth, or is something else happening?

After slipping into Building Three, Chen Ge repositioned the cleaver for easy access. If anything surprised him, he could draw it instantly. He spent half an hour climbing the stairs and familiarizing himself with the layout. There’s no basement, only twenty-three floors. Why does the elevator display twenty-four numbers?

He had no answer. Remembering Wang Xin’s mother’s warning, he avoided the elevator and eventually returned to the thirteenth floor. Inspector Lee would handle Xin Kang Apartments; Chen Ge’s task was to watch Room Three.

If Patient No. 2 truly lived in Room 3133, the white figure was probably the entity possessing her.

Creatures from behind the door needed living hosts to survive in this world, creating a kind of symbiosis. The corridor lay silent; most tenants on the floor had already moved away.

I wonder if I can run into the white shadow tonight.

Looking down the corridor, he noticed an open door spilling light into the darkness.

Someone’s home?As Chen Ge approached, his unease grew. Wait—isn’t this Room 3133?

The advertisement had been torn down, crumpled, and tossed onto the floor. Chen Ge peered inside. Sparse furniture stood on tiled floors, and a curtain divided the living room in two.

Has the owner returned?He had spent half an hour exploring the building after leaving Xin Kang Apartments, so it was possible. He waited outside for two minutes, but no sound came from within.

Drawing the cleaver, Chen Ge eased the door open and slipped inside. He restored it to its original angle and took care not to leave footprints.

The apartment was small, but two details stood out: an oversized bathtub in the bathroom and, beside the refrigerator, a locked freezer in the kitchen.

Is it hiding a body?

No other explanation seemed plausible. Every interior door stood open. Leaving the kitchen, Chen Ge entered the bedroom. Dark coats hung in the wardrobe, and a large, worn leather suitcase rested on top. Just as he rose onto his toes to pull it down, high heels clicked along the corridor outside.

He glanced around, then climbed into the wardrobe with his backpack. If they find me, it’s over.

Through the narrow gap between the wardrobe doors, Chen Ge watched the front door swing open. A man and woman stood outside. The man entered first, carrying a baton. He wore a security uniform and appeared to be in his twenties.

“You really saw the white shadow?”

“Yes, about half an hour ago. As I opened my door, something white flashed out of the elevator! I panicked, left my door open, and ran into the stairwell.”

The woman behind him wore red heels and fashionable clothes. Slight of build, with lustrous black hair, she concealed her face behind a mask.

Chen Ge had encountered them both that night. The man was Gu Feiyu, the new night guard; the woman was the masked stranger who had ridden down from the thirteenth floor and hurried into the parking garage.

“Stay here. I’ll check the elevator.” Gu Feiyu was not merely direct; he was courageous.

“Don’t leave me here alone…” The woman pulled on Gu Feiyu’s uniform.

“I won’t go far.” Unmoved by her fear, Gu Feiyu took his baton and flashlight to the elevator. He searched every corner but found no trace of the white figure.

“Could you have imagined it?”

“Impossible.” Her voice trembled. “Do you think it entered my apartment?”

She remained behind Gu Feiyu, staring at her open door without daring to approach.

“The captain says this place is haunted. If you’re so frightened, you should move,” Gu Feiyu said bluntly. “The previous tenant was insane. Whoever sold you the apartment may have cheated you.”

“I didn’t buy it. The ‘insane woman’ you mentioned was my older sister. After she disappeared, the apartment was transferred to me.” Her expression dimmed. “Everyone calls her mad, but no one in this world ever treated me with greater kindness.”

The woman entered, her heels striking sharply against the tile. “Don’t stand out there. If the door stays open, something might slip inside.”

“It’s okay. I still need to return to my patrol.”

“Please help me search for the white figure. Once we know it isn’t here, you can leave.” She pulled Gu Feiyu inside and shut the door.

“Okay…”

Gu Feiyu crossed the living room toward the balcony while the woman entered the bedroom. As she approached, Chen Ge held his breath. If she opened the wardrobe now, she would receive an unforgettable surprise.

After closing the bedroom door, she sat at the vanity and removed her mask before the mirror. She took several bottles and jars from a drawer and touched up her makeup. When finished, she slipped a small plastic container into her pocket and left.

“I’ve checked the bedroom; the white shadow is not in there.”

As she turned, Chen Ge glimpsed her face. Beneath the pallor, she looked hauntingly familiar.
